around.headline: Bengaluru police rearrest a convict who used a forged Supreme Court order to stay free for six years
around.summary: A life-term convict evaded prison for six years using a forged Supreme Court order before Bengaluru police caught up with and rearrested him, per The Times of India. It's a reminder that even official-looking court paperwork can be faked — if you ever need to verify a court order (for a case, a property dispute, anything), cross-check it on the court's e-courts portal rather than taking the document at face value.

around.headline: Heavy festival-week traffic and toll-plaza queues build up around Bengaluru ahead of Ganesh Chaturthi
around.summary: Thousands are heading to hometowns for the extended Gowri-Ganesha weekend, with heavy traffic reported into the city and long queues building at toll plazas on the Mysuru-Bengaluru highway, per Udayavani and Star of Mysore. If you're driving out of town this week, budget significant extra time at highway tolls or consider travelling a day early or late to dodge the peak rush.

around.headline: BMTC launches a revamped 'Namma BMTC 2.0' app and rolls out the NCMC card for bus and metro
around.summary: BMTC has launched an updated Namma BMTC 2.0 app alongside the NCMC (National Common Mobility Card), letting commuters tap the same card across bus and metro, per Inshorts. Worth setting up before your next commute if you're tired of juggling separate metro and bus tickets.

around.headline: Experts and protesters push back on Bengaluru's ₹17,700-crore Hebbal tunnel road over groundwater and park-land concerns
around.summary: Environmental researchers say there's 'little case' for the tunnel and warn it could disrupt groundwater and worsen flooding, while a Lalbagh-area protest is pushing to reroute the project's entry/exit points away from park land, per Deccan Herald and Mongabay India. If you live or commute near Hebbal, Lalbagh or the proposed corridor, this is worth tracking before construction plans are finalised.

around.headline: Karnataka allows kin to appear on behalf of elderly, sick and overseas voters during the SIR process
around.summary: Election authorities have clarified that family members can now appear at Special Intensive Revision (SIR) hearings for voters who are elderly, unwell or living abroad, per The Times of India. If you have an elderly or NRI relative on Bengaluru's voter rolls, you can now handle their SIR paperwork for them instead of the process requiring their personal presence.

around.headline: ED says Karnataka minister Satish Jarkiholi's family funnelled bribe money into gold assets abroad
around.summary: The Enforcement Directorate has alleged that money linked to bribes was funnelled by minister Satish Jarkiholi's family into buying gold assets in Africa, per The Times of India. It's a reminder that large, hard-to-trace asset purchases like gold are a common route for laundering illicit money — a pattern worth knowing if you ever handle due diligence on a business or investment partner.

around.headline: Xi Jinping and other BRICS leaders meet Modi in Delhi as the summit adopts a New Delhi declaration
around.summary: China's Xi Jinping travelled to Delhi for talks with PM Modi as the 11-nation BRICS summit adopted a New Delhi declaration, with Modi also holding separate talks with Putin and Iran's president, per Reuters and AP News. For Bengaluru's IT- and trade-heavy economy, deeper BRICS coordination on payments (flagged as a finance-track discussion, not a common currency) is a trend worth watching alongside the parallel EU-India trade talks.

street_smart.title: You ride to a crowded market to buy Ganesh Chaturthi decorations, and every marked parking slot is full. A young man waves you toward a stretch of pavement, says he'll 'keep an eye' on your bike for ₹20, and hands you a torn ticket stub. You're in a hurry. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: No single scam or safety incident in today's feeds carries enough detail for a standalone scenario, so this rotates to an evergreen topic — two-wheeler theft prevention, sharpened for festival-week crowding — not used as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks. Today's feeds do show unusually heavy festival traffic and market crowding around Ganesh Chaturthi, exactly the conditions when opportunistic bike theft spikes.
street_smart.situation: It's peak festival shopping hours, foot traffic is dense, and there's no BBMP-marked or shop-run parking area within sight.

choices.text: Lock the steering yourself regardless of the ticket, and loop a portable chain or disc lock through the wheel if you're carrying one.
choices.feedback: Correct. A steering lock — ideally backed by a chain or disc lock — is real deterrence: most opportunistic thieves move on rather than spend the extra 30-60 seconds it takes to defeat a second lock. Nobody's promise, paid or not, replaces that.

choices.text: Skip locking the steering since the watchman said he'd keep an eye on it, and just hand over ₹20 for the ticket.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. It's exactly how curbside bike theft works: an unlocked bike plus an unaccountable stranger's promise. The ticket stub isn't linked to any registered service — if the bike's gone when you're back, there's no one to hold responsible and nothing for police to act on.

choices.text: Lock the steering as usual, but don't bother looking for a shop-adjacent spot or any CCTV coverage — you're only running in for a few minutes.
choices.feedback: Risky. Locking the steering is the right instinct, but leaving the bike on a stretch with no shop or camera nearby still gives a patient thief time to work on the lock unnoticed. When a shop-adjacent or marked spot is even slightly farther, it's usually worth the extra few steps.

choices.text: Refuse the watchman entirely and ride around hunting for an official parking spot even if it takes 15+ minutes.
choices.feedback: Risky. Refusing the watchman is fine, but you don't need to burn 15+ minutes hunting for an official lot — a steering-locked bike on a well-trafficked stretch is usually safe enough. The lock is the protection, not the parking authority.

takeaways: A steering lock — ideally backed by a portable chain or disc lock — is the real protection; pay or don't pay a self-appointed 'watchman', but always lock the bike yourself.
A handwritten 'parking ticket' from an unregistered attendant has no legal standing; if the bike still gets stolen, file an FIR immediately — it's required for any insurance claim.
Keep a photo of your RC (registration, engine and chassis numbers) on your phone so you have those details ready fast for an FIR or insurance claim.

quiz.question: A Bengaluru convict serving a life term stayed free for six years using what, before police rearrested him today?
quiz.why: The forged order was used to secure his release; the case highlights why court documents — like any official paperwork — should be verified through the court's own e-courts portal rather than taken at face value.

quiz.question: The Enforcement Directorate accused Karnataka minister Satish Jarkiholi's family of funnelling bribe money into which kind of asset abroad?
quiz.why: Gold is a classic vehicle for laundering illicit money because it's easy to move, hard to trace, and holds value across borders without leaving a clear paper trail.

quiz.question: Today's BRICS summit in New Delhi, where Xi Jinping and Modi held talks, was described by AP News as a summit of how many nations?
quiz.why: BRICS has expanded well beyond its original five founding members (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) to include newer members like Iran, the UAE, Egypt and Ethiopia.

quiz.question: Karnataka's western coastline lies along which sea?
quiz.why: The Arabian Sea coastline gives Karnataka major ports like Mangaluru's New Mangalore Port, a key gateway for the state's trade even though Bengaluru itself is inland.

quiz.question: Which interest rate does the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee set to manage inflation and liquidity in the economy?
quiz.why: The repo rate is what the RBI charges commercial banks for short-term loans; raising it makes borrowing costlier economy-wide, which is the RBI's main lever for cooling inflation.
